newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end up, led by old crop on exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end up, led by old crop on exports.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended higher Thursday, led by old-crop months amid talk export business was picking up following the recent sell-off, pit sources said.

"There was talk about exports of old crop beans and that helped August lead the charge here," said Dave Armstrong, analyst for ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp. "We're now competitive with Brazil on oil, close on meal and in August beans," he said.
Rumors circulated on the trading floor that a cargo of U.S. old crop soybeans was sold for August shipment from the U.S. Gulf, traders said.
Exporters could not confirm the rumor but some said the deal was likely given recent price moves.
Trade sources and analysts noted U.S. prices had fallen nearly $2.00 per bushel since May's 8-1/2 year highs. Meanwhile, Brazilian basis levels have firmed.

"I think what's happened is that the Brazilian basis has firmed up and our price has dropped which makes us competitive from August 1 forward," said Roy Huckabay, vice-president of LIT Investor Services.
Soybeans settled 17-1/4 to 4-1/2 cents higher, with August up 17-1/4 at $6.87-1/2 a bushel.
USDA weekly export sales data was also deemed supportive. USDA Thursday said net export sales of old crop soybeans during the week ended June 26 totalled 17,800 tonnes.
Many trade sources had expected a negative number as world buyers were shifting old crop purchases to new crop in anticipation of a bumper crop this fall.
Weather patterns remain conducive for new crop development with weekend forecasts calling for cool weather and showers across much of the U.S. Midwest.
Volume was said to be thin ahead of the three-day Independence Day holiday weekend beginning on Friday.

On the day, funds bought at least seven million bushels, divided nearly equally between the November and August. Refco Inc bought 2.5 million bushels August and 1.5 million November, Iowa Grain bought three million November and FIMAT Futures bought 2.5 million November.

Players continued to liquidate the July contract ahead of the July 22 expiry but most of the exit orders were in the form of spreads, floor sources said. Goldenberg-Hehmeyer spread 500,000 bushels July/August at 39 cents, premium July, SAK Futures spread 300,000 August/July at 42 cents, and Prudential Securities spread 200,000 July/Nov at 128 cents.
The July/Nov spread closed at $1.30 a bushel, premium July, up 4-1/2 cents from Wednesday's close.

In options trade, Smith Barney bought 300 August $7.25 calls at five cents and 200 August $7.50 calls at four cents. Produce Grain sold 300 November $6.25 calls at 14 cents and sold 300 November $600 calls and 21 cents.
Volatility in the August closed at 33-3/4 percent and November at 19-1/2 percent.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 55,000 contracts, well below the 79,556 contracts traded on Wednesday.
